texts.252g-P13o1: There is a difficult paradox to consider. The need for new members in a small community is greater, but the ability of that community to tolerate the disruption of new members is less. Whether there are eight people in the community or eighty, someone still has to grow the food, fix the cars, balance the books, watch the kids, and maintain the water system. The water well doesn’t care how beautiful someone’s heart is.
texts.252g-P13o1P14n1:
There is a difficult paradox to consider. The need for new members in a small community is greater, but the ability of that community to tolerate the disruption of new members is less. Whether there are eight people in the community or eighty, someone still has to grow the food, fix the cars, balance the books, watch the kids, and maintain the water system. The water well doesn’t care how beautiful someone’s heart is.

So early on, members usually need to have more resource than acute need, and some skill to contribute, and a willingness to learn.
texts.252g-U8x:
This community may not be a good fit for you right now if:

You’re running from some crisis right now and mainly need a place to land, get treatment, housing, legal aid, etc. (A founding group shouldn’t pretend it can give you those.)

You want all of the benefits of village life but don’t want to take on governance, maintenance, conflict, care, etc.

You’re not willing to look at yourself when jealousy or conflict comes up.

You have a need that far outstrips your ability to bring in a resource for it right now. (This doesn’t mean you’re bad or doomed, it’s about timing; it may mean you need to take a first step of finding support where you are so you can build up your resources.)

(There should be ways of not flat-out rejecting people who fall into these categories, like saying “later,” or “in another role,” or “with more support.”)
texts.252g-P15n2P16fL1w2:
How to use the framing of “I don’t have the capacity to…” without it becoming a respectable way to exclude disabled people, poor people, people who aren’t very articulate or don’t have the language of therapy at their fingertips, people who are simply not convenient – I don’t know. It’s not going to be solved by pretending it’s unlimited; that’s going to require actually making concrete criteria, allowing for outside review, allowing for re-visiting a “not now” decision, and all of that. And even then, the power is dangerous.
